poi_name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Leave Wall Street behind — the Federal Reserve Bank of New York is about eight minutes ahead.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Here's a question worth chewing on as you walk: what happens when a whole country's money rests on one man's nerve?","source_id":"a0a1807e-57d6-4815-869c-2323a2727525","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"In 1907, that man was J. P. Morgan, who personally mobilized enough banking support to stave off a collapse that could have rivaled the Great Depression — and seven years later, in 1914, the Federal Reserve was created so a central bank, not a single tycoon, would make that call.","source_id":"a0a1807e-57d6-4815-869c-2323a2727525","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The building in front of you went up like a fortress in 1924, and it's no New York snobbery to call it the most significant of the thirteen Federal Reserve sites.","source_id":"a0a1807e-57d6-4815-869c-2323a2727525","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Look at the limestone as you pass — it weathers in different tones, shifting light to dark — and those magnificent wrought-iron lanterns are the work of Philadelphia's Samuel Yellin.","source_id":"a0a1807e-57d6-4815-869c-2323a2727525","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Nearby, Federal Hall, a Greek Revival masterpiece, holds a museum devoted to postcolonial New York.","source_id":"fc4c7e50-814c-4bf6-bd0a-7757d8030f32","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"But the real story is eighty feet down.","source_id":"22fbc5a6-3820-4837-96d1-e2f89db8995d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Descend to the basement of this financial fortress and you'll see more lucre than you ever will again in your life — behind a door a good five feet thick sits a gold vault straight out of Mission: Impossible.","source_id":"22fbc5a6-3820-4837-96d1-e2f89db8995d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"It holds upward of $110 billion in bullion — about a quarter of the official monetary gold of eighty countries, a full twenty-five percent of all the gold reserves on Earth, and far more than is kept in Fort Knox.","source_id":"39ae56af-ce43-4951-a996-db16f1b9d16c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4,"also_cites":["22fbc5a6-3820-4837-96d1-e2f89db8995d"]},{"text":"Ninety-five percent of it belongs to foreign nations, who trust it here because, embedded in the bedrock of Manhattan and guarded by a small army of marksmen with their own on-site firing range, it's considered the safest place in the world for such storage.","source_id":"22fbc5a6-3820-4837-96d1-e2f89db8995d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"And how do they move it from one country's room to the next? Wheelbarrows — still.","source_id":"39ae56af-ce43-4951-a996-db16f1b9d16c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"No currency has been printed here since that function moved to New Jersey in 1992.","source_id":"22fbc5a6-3820-4837-96d1-e2f89db8995d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"If you want to see it for yourself, the hour-long, reservation-only tour at 33 Liberty Street takes you into the gold vault and the bank's museum, where money from all over the world is on display.","source_id":"645fd515-c98b-49fb-b14d-6e8ac3b3fa16","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4}]}
